book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: After end of month see Boris ski out in Siberian location

parts.note: Nov, short for November, the month that closes autumn near the end of the year

indicators.note: the letters of Boris ski come out of their order and are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the month is over, watch Boris go skiing somewhere in Siberia.
explanation.walkthrough: After and see only join the pieces: the month comes first, then the scrambled letters follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Novosibirsk is the largest city in Siberia, on the river Ob.

clue.text: Anything in Manhattan etc that's lewd?

indicators.note: the word for anything goes inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: Manhattan and the other boroughs make up New York, NY
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A question whether everything in Manhattan is risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty can mean mildly indecent or titillating, as in a naughty postcard.

clue.text: Very short pronouncement in a language few of us understand

definitions.text: a language few of us understand

indicators.note: the decree is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an edict is an official decree

explanation.surface: A curt statement made in some obscure tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Vedic is the ancient form of Sanskrit in which the Vedas were composed, understood by few scholars.

clue.text: Rugby player has to run into school hospital

indicators.note: the run goes inside the school sick bay

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, is a boarding school's sick bay
a race is a run

explanation.surface: A rugby player must hurry to the school's medical room after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Saracens is a leading English rugby club, so a Saracen is one of its players.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Saracens club side is called a Saracen, after the club's name.

clue.text: African fellow given rotten holiday, keeping hot

indicators.note: the busman holds the letter for hot inside

parts.note: a busman's holiday is a dreary break spent doing one's usual job, so a busman is the fellow given one

explanation.surface: An African man stuck with a miserable holiday in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: A busman's holiday is a British idiom for a break spent doing the same thing as one's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushman is a traditional name for a member of the San peoples of southern Africa.

clue.text: Seeing and respecting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: looking at or observing
second meaning: about or concerning, a preposition

explanation.walkthrough: Respecting here is not about esteem; it means with respect to.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gazing at something and concerning a topic, as in regarding your letter.

clue.text: What is missing from girl's story book — something like cricket

indicators.note: the first word of the title is dropped from it

parts.note: What Katy Did, Susan Coolidge's classic girls' novel
the very word removed

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a girls' book, then an abrupt turn to cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket wants to be the bat-and-ball game; it is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The katydid is a green bush cricket of North America, named for its call.

clue.text: A northern city with land separated out into pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word land is split off and taken away from the end of the city's name

parts.note: Sunderland is a city in north-east England
taken as written, the very letters removed

explanation.surface: A northern city whose territory has been carved up and parcelled out.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is Sunderland, and the clue spells out that its last four letters are the ones to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn asunder means broken apart into separate parts, so the adverb matches into pieces.

clue.text: Plant associated with sewer originally?

definitions.meaning: sewer means one who sews, not a drain; the plant's name links it to a needle
the first man in Genesis sewed fig leaves, making him the original sewer

explanation.walkthrough: Sewer reads as a drain but means a person who sews; Adam and Eve sewed fig leaves together in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's needle is a yucca, a spiky ornamental shrub of the agave family.

clue.text: Having a particular sense located in the ear

indicators.note: heard rather than read, the word for located gives the sound of the answer

parts.note: sited means placed or located

explanation.surface: Something with a special sense placed inside the ear, like a hearing organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at hearing, but the sense in question is vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A sighted person possesses vision, one particular sense among the five.

clue.text: Elk arrested — result of my working?

definitions.text: Elk arrested — result of my working?

indicators.note: the letters are put to work and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunter boasts that a stopped elk is the product of their labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A deerstalker hunts deer by creeping up on them, so a brought-down elk is their handiwork.

clue.text: A hospital brought in medic on a casual basis

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the hospital's letter is taken inside the word for medic

parts.note: doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A hospital calls in a doctor as a temporary, casual arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc arrangements are improvised for the occasion rather than planned or permanent.

clue.text: Conservative rural community, a place giving opportunity for academic study

definitions.text: a place giving opportunity for academic study

parts.note: Ambridge is the fictional village in The Archers, the long-running BBC radio farming soap

explanation.surface: A Tory village, yet somewhere offering the chance to study at university level.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambridge is the village of The Archers, a BBC radio soap about country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is home to one of the world's oldest universities, a seat of scholarship.

clue.text: Squalid place — huge, endlessly dark and dismal

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, any filthy dwelling

indicators.note: the word for huge loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: giant used as an adjective

explanation.surface: A grim description of a slum: vast, gloomy and depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes Squalid place look like the thing being defined; it is only the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian, from the river Styx of the underworld, describes extreme gloom and darkness.

clue.text: Tetchy bishop hemmed in by two from Rome in front of altar?

indicators.note: everything before is placed ahead of the altar
the bishop's letters are enclosed between the two ones

parts.note: two Roman numeral ones
RR, Right Reverend, a bishop's title
the communion table

explanation.surface: A grumpy bishop flanked by two Romans standing before the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: The two from Rome are numerals rather than people.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and tetchy are synonyms for easily annoyed and bad-tempered.

clue.text: A dean is naughty on account of the nymphs

indicators.note: letters that misbehave are jumbled out of their proper order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean misbehaves because of some alluring nymphs.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiades is the classical plural of naiad, a water nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: Pig run into by artist in African town

indicators.note: the pig is entered by the artist, which ends up inside it

parts.note: an elt is a young sow, a dialect word
Gustave Doré, the French illustrator

explanation.surface: A painter collides with a pig somewhere in an African town.
explanation.walkthrough: Elt, a young female pig, is an old word known mainly from crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldoret is a sizeable town in the highlands of western Kenya.

clue.text: Swimmers almost expected to get medals

indicators.note: the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: due, as in the train is due
gongs is slang for medals or decorations

explanation.surface: Competitive swimmers are tipped to win medals.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmers looks like athletes; they are sea mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dugongs are large herbivorous marine mammals, sea cows of the Indian Ocean and Pacific.

clue.text: Silly lout seen leaving square with solvent

indicators.note: a silly arrangement scrambles the letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for square departs from the word seen

parts.note: taken as written
S stands for square, as in a street name

explanation.surface: A foolish yob is spotted walking out of a town square carrying solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Toluene is a colourless liquid hydrocarbon widely used as an industrial solvent and thinner.

clue.text: Main purpose of arts graduate tackling one French author

indicators.note: the graduate grapples with the other pieces by wrapping round them

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts
I is the Roman numeral for one
André Gide, Nobel-winning novelist

explanation.surface: An arts graduate's central aim in taking on a French writer for a thesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The big idea is the overall goal or central concept behind a plan.

clue.text: Head of state I fix military code

parts.note: George Bush, a US president
taken as written
do, as in do up or sort out

explanation.surface: A president claims to set the rules for the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan lost the I, which the wordplay needs between the president and the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai's code of honour, the way of the Japanese warrior.

clue.text: Casually visits bishop restricted by medical condition

indicators.note: the bishop's letter is confined inside the illness

parts.note: dropsy, an old name for oedema

explanation.surface: A bishop with a medical problem pays informal calls.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop by is to call on someone informally without arranging it beforehand.

clue.text: From which one could imply that old-fashioned TV isn't a drug?

definitions.text: From which one could imply that old-fashioned TV isn't
definitions.meaning: split after its seventh letter the answer reads as a claim about modern sets, implying older sets lacked that technology
the straight sense: a heart medicine made from foxgloves

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer makes a statement about modern broadcasting; read as one it names a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is a heart stimulant extracted from foxglove leaves, a long-established drug.

clue.text: Criticise site of airport

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to disparage or find fault with
second meaning: ... in County Mayo, Ireland, home of Ireland West Airport

explanation.walkthrough: Knock is a small Irish pilgrimage town whose airport was built in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a verb for running something down and as the Irish place name.

clue.text: Material in a river caught in two duck's tails

indicators.note: these pieces are held between the two tail letters

parts.note: the last letter of duck, twice
taken as written
the Po, Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Some fabric snagged in a river, tangled round the tails of two ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapok is the silky fibre from a tropical tree, used as stuffing material.

clue.text: Honour due to some men (no blemishes)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run inside them

parts.note: the run of letters sits across the end of men, all of no and the start of blemishes

explanation.surface: An honour owed to certain men whose records are spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, or more loosely to dignify them.

clue.text: Confession of dandy who insists on his own way?

definitions.text: who insists on his own way
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: one who insists on his own way

parts.note: a confession admits what one is, starting I'm
a poser is someone who poses for effect, a show-off in fine clothes

explanation.surface: A dandy owns up to being someone who always gets his way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as a dandy's admission, I'm poser.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposer forces his will or demands on others, getting his own way.

clue.text: The master doing the business in the opening movement

definitions.meaning: read as a person in charge, but it is a master key that opens every lock

definitions.text: doing the business in the opening movement
definitions.meaning: sounds like a conductor at the start of a symphony; it is a key turning in a lock

explanation.walkthrough: The musical picture of a maestro in a first movement hides a key at work opening a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key has its wards filed away so it can open many different locks, like a master key.
